label: In the last trials of an episode, the gate drops when S1 is reached (most after a1) and after no reward.
terms: (in_state == 1) * (action == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 3) ;; (phase != D2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 3) ;; (in_state == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 3) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 3) ;; np.exp((ep_trial - 99) / 3) * (tv("state", -1) == 1) * (phase != D2)
explanation: The update gate z of unit 35 stays near 1 (it holds its state) for most of the episode. Beyond the timing baseline, it drops sharply in the last ~10 trials of the episode, with a ramp that grows roughly exponentially toward trial 99. The drop is largest at D2 when S1 is shown, especially after an a1 choice (common a1->S1), and at D1/GO after an unrewarded trial. Away from the episode end the effects are small: about -0.01 at D1 after a1->S2 (rare), and a weak negative dependence on belief_lo at D2 (lower when the observer favours S1). The free fit adds these small terms plus a carry-over from the last trial reaching S1, going from about 0.42 to 0.48 on dev. Every term is observed (in_state and action are known at D2), so no future variables are used. The profile additive ceiling is only 0.17 because it has no term for the late-episode interaction; that interaction is the main finding.

issues: The recorded short form reproduces: test R^2 beyond timing 0.424 (weights -0.195 for S1 after a1, -0.059 for unrewarded at D1/GO, -0.085 for S1), which is 88% of the free fit's 0.484. The D2 S1 drop is real: dropping the in_state==1 term costs about 0.016, and dropping the a1 interaction costs 0.08 (0.341 without it). So 'S1, most after a1' holds: the summed weight is -0.28 for common a1->S1 and -0.085 for rare a2->S1.

The label's D1/GO claim ('after no reward') is incomplete. Swapping the reward term for (phase != D2)*(prev_action == 1)*ramp scores better (0.437 vs 0.424 on test). With both in the fit their weights are about equal (-0.040 and -0.046; 4-term test score 0.454). So at D1 and GO the drop follows a previous a1 choice as much as a previous non-reward.
The time constant is not tuned: /4 scores slightly better than /3 (0.432 vs 0.424), and /2 is worse (0.374). The ramp shape is robust, not curve fitting.

Misses show no large systematic class. The mean error by phase is at most 0.001, and the biggest cells are about 0.01 (D1 after a1->S2 over-predicted by about -0.012, D2 after a2 under-predicted by about +0.007). These are small next to the late-episode drops of 0.1 to 0.3.

The worst-fit windows are all late episodes (t92-99) with long a1->S1 streaks. There the gate sits about 0.05-0.1 below the prediction even at GO, so the drop builds up across a run of trials in a way the per-step terms do not capture. This is a remaining limitation, not a refutation.
No future variables are used: in_state and action are only used at D2, where they are observed.
